label.description: Construct an exact, case-sensitive disk label group handle from a STRING expression. Computed names such as label("chest" + $index) are supported; integer concatenation uses signed decimal text. Names must be nonempty, <=256 characters, valid Unicode and have no surrounding whitespace. The handle selects locations rather than capturing contents. Dynamic programs use one bounded complete label snapshot per invocation; unavailable groups are not empty. Constructor name ignores case.
label.example:
let index = 1
let source = label("chest" + index)

item.description: Construct an item filter from one quoted source literal. An exact, case-sensitive registry ID matches every metadata/NBT variant of that item; '*' matches all items. This is a RESOURCE_SELECTOR, not an exact ITEM_KEY. No item: prefix, metadata suffix, glob pattern, NBT filter or fluid selector is accepted. Unknown valid IDs match nothing; the constructor name ignores case.

ore.description: Construct an OreDictionary filter from one exact, case-sensitive quoted source literal of 1–256 ASCII letters, digits or underscores. Registered alternatives and wildcard metadata registrations are supported. Unknown names match nothing and do not register a new ore category. No ore: prefix, pattern or computed string is accepted. This is a RESOURCE_SELECTOR, not an exact ITEM_KEY; the constructor name ignores case.

array.description: Construct a homogeneous dynamic array with one exact element type. A quoted compile-time type literal such as array("integer") creates a typed empty integer[]; fixed/dynamic dimensions and struct element types are supported, but VOID is not. The literal is limited to 1024 characters and type depth 32. Any sequence value can be explicitly copied: fixed/dynamic arrays or captured ITEM_CONTENTS/ITEM_LOCATIONS/FLUID_CONTENTS, preserving the exact element type. No implicit fixed/dynamic conversion is performed, and an untyped [] remains invalid. Dynamic length is a value property, with at most 256 outer entries and 4096 actual retained logical cells including nested children. Dynamic arrays can be STATE when every nested element is persistable (integer, boolean, string or a collection of those); handles and snapshots remain RAM-only. STATE bounds actual aggregate cells, strings and serialized disk bytes before replacement. Values are immutable copies; construction/replacement walks the outer entries in O(n), under shared work/allocation and retained payload limits. Constructor name ignores case.
array.example:
let values = array("integer")
let seeded = array([1, 2])

signatures: push(ref values: T[], value: T) -> void
push.description: Append one exact-type element through an explicit writable REF dynamic-array target. This VOID operation is a standalone statement, not a value expression. It installs an immutable replacement in O(n) outer entries; ordinary value copies keep their prior contents. Maximum length is 256 and actual retained logical cells are limited to 4096, with shared work/allocation and retained payload limits. Fixed arrays are not accepted; persistable dynamic STATE targets obey aggregate cell/string/disk limits before replacement; the element type never changes. Whole-array references stay valid, but captured indexed references/assignments can become stale after structural replacement, including a same-length or ABA replacement or whole-root rebind. Invalidation is conservative across the dynamic-containing root, so sibling indexed references may also fault; a successful writer refreshes itself. Earlier RHS effects are not rolled back by a stale assignment fault. REF effects cannot run in program-wide LET initializers or named-redstone subscription expressions. Operation name ignores case.

pop.description: Remove and return the final element through an explicit writable REF dynamic-array target. An empty array faults. The result has the array's exact element type; fixed arrays are not accepted. Persistable dynamic STATE targets obey aggregate cell/string/disk limits before replacement. The operation installs an immutable replacement in O(n) outer entries, leaving ordinary value copies unchanged, under the 256-entry/4096-actual-cell and shared work/allocation/retained payload limits. Whole-array references remain valid. Captured indexed references or assignments can fault after structural replacement, including same-length replacement, ABA changes and whole-root rebinds; conservative root-wide invalidation can affect siblings too. A successful writer refreshes itself. A stale assignment fault does not roll back RHS effects already committed. REF effects cannot run in program-wide LET initializers or named-redstone subscription expressions. Operation name ignores case.
pop.example:
let values = array([1, 2])
let last = pop(ref values)

signatures: extend(ref values: T[], sequence: sequence<T>) -> void
extend.description: Append every captured source entry in order through an explicit writable REF dynamic-array target. The source may be a fixed/dynamic array or native contents/location sequence with exactly the same element type. This VOID operation is a standalone statement. An empty source is a no-op and does not change the structural epoch. Otherwise it installs an immutable O(n) outer replacement under the 256-entry/4096-actual-cell and shared work/allocation/retained payload limits; ordinary copies remain unchanged. Structural replacement can invalidate captured indexed references across the dynamic-containing root, including siblings and ABA/rebind changes; whole-array refs stay valid and a successful writer refreshes itself. A stale assignment fault does not roll back committed RHS effects. REF effects cannot run in program-wide LET initializers or named-redstone subscription expressions. Operation name ignores case.

signatures: insert(ref values: T[], index: integer, value: T) -> void
insert.description: Insert one exact-type element before a zero-based index through an explicit writable REF dynamic-array target. The index must be in 0..len(values), inclusive; insertion at len(values) appends. This VOID operation is a standalone statement. It installs an immutable O(n) outer replacement, shifting later entries, under the 256-entry/4096-actual-cell and shared work/allocation/retained payload limits. Ordinary copies remain unchanged. Structural replacement can invalidate indexed references across the root, including siblings and same-length/ABA/rebind changes; whole-array refs remain valid and a successful writer refreshes itself. Stale assignment faults do not undo committed RHS effects. REF effects cannot run in program-wide LET initializers or named-redstone subscription expressions. Operation name ignores case.

signatures: removeAt(ref values: T[], index: integer) -> T
removeat.description: Remove and return the exact-type element at a zero-based index through an explicit writable REF dynamic-array target. The index must be in 0..len(values)-1; empty arrays and negative/out-of-range indices fault. It installs an immutable O(n) outer replacement, shifting later entries, under shared work/allocation and the normal 256-entry/4096-actual-cell/retained payload limits. Ordinary copies keep their prior contents. Structural replacement can invalidate indexed references across the root, including siblings and same-length/ABA/rebind changes; whole-array refs remain valid and a successful writer refreshes itself. A stale assignment fault does not undo committed RHS effects. REF effects cannot run in program-wide LET initializers or named-redstone subscription expressions. Operation name ignores case.
removeat.example:
let values = array([1, 2, 3])
let removed = removeAt(ref values, 1)

clear.description: Replace a writable REF dynamic array with a typed empty value, preserving its exact element type. This VOID operation is a standalone statement. Clearing an empty array is a no-op and does not change the structural epoch. Ordinary copies retain their contents; replacement uses immutable value semantics and shared work/allocation/retained payload limits. Structural replacement can invalidate captured indexed references across the dynamic-containing root, including siblings and same-length/ABA/rebind changes; whole-array refs stay valid and a successful writer refreshes itself. A stale assignment fault does not roll back committed RHS effects. REF effects cannot run in program-wide LET initializers or named-redstone subscription expressions. Operation name ignores case.

peek.description: Return the final captured element without changing the sequence. Accepts fixed/dynamic arrays and native ITEM_CONTENTS/ITEM_LOCATIONS/FLUID_CONTENTS sequences by value, not REF, and returns their exact element type. An empty sequence faults. Does not rescan inventories or install a structural replacement. Shared expression work limits apply. Operation name ignores case.

contains.description: Return whether any captured sequence element deeply matches an item of exactly the declared element type. Accepts fixed/dynamic arrays and native ITEM_CONTENTS/ITEM_LOCATIONS/FLUID_CONTENTS by value, not REF. Empty sequences return false. Membership compares exact typed values: case-sensitive strings, complete label names/side/slot restrictions, selector kinds and exact item/fluid NBT keys, with recursive array/struct contents. The scan and deep comparisons consume shared work limits without rescanning inventories. This membership rule does not add collection equality to == or !=. Operation name ignores case.

indexof.description: Return the first zero-based captured index whose element deeply matches an item of exactly the declared element type, or -1 if absent, including an empty sequence. Accepts fixed/dynamic arrays and native ITEM_CONTENTS/ITEM_LOCATIONS/FLUID_CONTENTS by value, not REF. Matching uses exact typed values, including case-sensitive strings, complete label side/slot restrictions, selector kinds, exact item/fluid NBT keys and recursive array/struct contents. The scan and comparisons consume shared work limits without rescanning inventories. This membership rule does not add collection equality to == or !=. Operation name ignores case.

min.description: Return the smaller of two signed 64-bit integers. Both arguments evaluate once, left to right. The built-in name ignores case; an exact-name player function takes precedence.

max.description: Return the larger of two signed 64-bit integers. Both arguments evaluate once, left to right. The built-in name ignores case; an exact-name player function takes precedence.

signatures: clamp(value: integer, low: integer, high: integer) -> integer
clamp.description: Restrict a signed 64-bit integer to the inclusive low/high bounds. Reversed bounds fault. Arguments evaluate once, left to right. The built-in name ignores case; an exact-name player function takes precedence.

abs.description: Return the absolute value of a signed 64-bit integer. The minimum signed value (-9223372036854775808) faults because its positive counterpart cannot fit. The built-in name ignores case; an exact-name player function takes precedence.

len.description: Return the outer entry count of a fixed or dynamic array or a captured native ITEM_CONTENTS/ITEM_LOCATIONS/FLUID_CONTENTS sequence, including zero. A dynamic array's logical length belongs to its value, not its T[] type. For a string, return its Unicode code-point count rather than UTF-8 bytes or displayed grapheme clusters. Does not rescan inventories. The built-in name ignores case; an exact-name player function takes precedence.
len.example:
let stock = label("inputs").contents()
if (len(stock) > 0) then
  print(stock[0].total)
end

total.description: Sum captured group totals or physical-location amounts using checked signed 64-bit arithmetic. Accepts native ITEM_CONTENTS/ITEM_LOCATIONS sequences, not ordinary arrays. Walks captured rows under shared work limits without rescanning inventories; overflow faults. The built-in name ignores case; an exact-name player function takes precedence.

stock.description: Read the captured total for one exact ITEM_KEY, or zero if absent. The key includes registry ID, metadata and canonical NBT; ITEM/ORE selectors are not accepted. Walks the captured groups under shared work limits without rescanning inventories. The built-in name ignores case; an exact-name player function takes precedence.
stock.example:
let snapshot = label("inputs").contents()
if (len(snapshot) > 0) then
  print(stock(snapshot, snapshot[0].item))
end

shortage.description: Return the additional amount needed: required minus available, clamped to zero. Both signed 64-bit integer arguments must be nonnegative or execution faults. This calculation does not query inventories. The built-in name ignores case; an exact-name player function takes precedence.

signatures: transfer(source: label_ref, destination: label_ref, amount: integer) [into $result]
transfer(source: label_ref, destination: label_ref, selection: resource_selector | item_key) [into $result]
transfer(source: label_ref, destination: label_ref, selection: resource_selector | item_key, amount: integer) [into $result]
transfer.description: The third argument may be an integer total item-count limit (all items), or an item key/selector (matching stock). Four arguments require an item key/selector followed by an integer amount. Use transferf for fluids, in millibuckets; this action stays item-only. An item-moving statement, not a value-returning function. Two arguments select all items; a third selector/key selects matching items, while a third integer caps all items; an omitted amount observes matching visible source stock. Four arguments provide one nonnegative aggregate cap across variants and containers. ITEM/ORE selectors are broad; an ITEM_KEY from contents() selects exact metadata/NBT. Optional INTO declares a fresh local record with integer requested/moved/remaining and string status (complete, partial, no_match, no_capacity or unavailable). Unavailable automatic preflight can report requested=0 without proving emptiness. Provider errors, exhausted work limits and recovery uncertainty fault; earlier confirmed transfers remain committed. Cannot appear inside a data expression or value-returning function; void procedures may use it. The statement name ignores case.

print.description: A debug-output statement accepting 1–8 typed expressions; it does not return a value. Arguments evaluate only while output capture is enabled and allowance remains. Use in triggers or void procedures; not in value-returning functions or data expressions. The statement name ignores case.

fluid.description: Select an exact Forge fluid registry name (water, lava or a mod registered name), or every fluid with *. Requires a quoted literal. Broad over NBT; captured FLUID_KEY values require exact fluid/NBT. Use with transferf and fqueries. Amounts are mB.

signatures: transferf(source: label_ref, destination: label_ref, amount: integer) [into $result]
transferf(source: label_ref, destination: label_ref, selection: resource_selector | fluid_key) [into $result]
transferf(source: label_ref, destination: label_ref, selection: resource_selector | fluid_key, amount: integer) [into $result]
transferf.description: Fluid action in millibuckets (1000 mB = one bucket). Missing amount means a finite visible matching-stock snapshot. Third integer caps all fluids; third FLUID selector/key filters stock; four arguments filter then cap. FLUID selectors are broad over NBT; FLUID_KEY is exact. Destination capacity, side permissions and shared action/work limits apply. Item slots are invalid. Optional INTO exposes requested/moved/remaining/status. Use in triggers or void procedures; not inside an expression or value-returning function. Unknown provider ownership is retained as recovery evidence and pauses execution.

wait.description: Statement: suspend the current trigger and active player-function stack for n game ticks. Does not block the server or other triggers. Locals, loop progress and completed expression operands survive; new firings of this busy trigger are not queued. Zero is a no-op; negatives/overflow fault. Resumes independently of original trigger interval. INPUT providers/retention refresh while prior quantity spending remains. Budgets refresh per invocation; retained memory is bounded. RAM-only continuation is cancelled on unload, reset, code/disk replacement or runtime fault. Allowed inside player-defined functions, but cannot return a value or initialize program-wide LET/STATE.

setcircuit.description: Explicit trigger/procedure action: set compatible connected GregTech ghost circuits to 1..24; 0/-1 clears. Uses native ghost configuration, never physical circuit transfer or guessed slots. Whole-machine labels only: no side/slot modifiers. Entire group is preflighted before writes. INTO declares matched/changed integer fields plus status string: complete, partial, unavailable or unsupported. Callback/work failures fault; already accepted configuration changes stay committed. Shares native action/query limits. Optional GregTech adapter; unsupported hosts are unchanged. Not an expression; permitted in triggers and void procedures.

break.description: Exit the innermost lexical counted/Java FOR, foreach or WHILE loop. Skips remaining body and Java FOR update; does not yield or roll back effects. Supported in triggers and player functions, including after WAIT. A function cannot break its caller loop. No arguments or labels. Outside-loop use is a compiler error. Text-only until a lossless Visual representation exists.
break.example: every 20 ticks { for i = 0 to 10 { if (i == 2) { break } print(i) } }

contents.description: Capture a read-only native sequence of exact visible-item groups from a LABEL_REF. Each group has item (ITEM_KEY including registry ID, metadata and NBT), id, metadata, total and locations (ITEM_LOCATIONS). Locations expose dimension/x/y/z/slot/sideMask/amount. An optional ITEM/ORE selector filters the scan; an exact ITEM_KEY is not accepted here. Complete empty access produces zero groups; missing, incomplete, unsupported or over-budget access faults without a partial result. Captured data is not a reservation or a live view, and cannot be stored in STATE. The method name ignores case; fields are case-sensitive.
contents.example:
let stock = label("inputs").contents(ore("ingotIron"))
for group in stock do
  print(group.id, group.metadata, group.total)
end

count.description: Count matching visible items in the current selected LABEL_REF view using checked signed 64-bit arithmetic. Requires one ITEM/ORE selector, not an exact ITEM_KEY. Counts visible stock even when extraction is refused; it is not a capacity or reservation check. Missing, incomplete, unsupported or over-budget access faults. The method name ignores case.
count.example:
let source = label("inputs")
if (source.available()) then
  print(source.count(item("minecraft:iron_ingot")))
end

empty.description: Return true only when the complete available LABEL_REF view contains no visible matching items. With no selector, checks all visible items. Missing, incomplete or unsupported access returns false; provider errors and exhausted work limits fault. Does not inspect fluids, free space or insertion capacity. An optional filter must be an ITEM/ORE selector, not an exact ITEM_KEY. The method name ignores case.
empty.example:
if (label("ped").empty()) then
  print("No visible pedestal items")
end

available.description: Check that the nonempty selected LABEL_REF group is connected, loaded and supported, with visible permitted inventory slots in every distinct view. Missing, incomplete, unsupported or entirely hidden access returns false; provider errors and exhausted work limits fault. This checks access, not matching stock, extraction permission, free space or insertion capacity. An optional ITEM/ORE selector does not change this access-only meaning. For native redstone ports use redstoneAvailable(). The method name ignores case.
available.example:
let source = label("inputs")
if (source.available()) then
  print(source.count(item("*")))
end

side.description: Return a new LABEL_REF restricted to one absolute physical block face. Requires a quoted source literal: down/up/north/south/west/east, with bottom/top aliases, ignoring case. Relative directions, NULL and computed strings are not accepted. Replaces the handle's previous side restriction while preserving its slots; leaves the original handle unchanged. Does not alter a separate INPUT/OUTPUT statement naming the same label. The method name ignores case.

slots.description: Return a new LABEL_REF restricted to an inclusive backend slot-index range. Bounds must satisfy 0 <= first <= last <= 2147483647 or execution faults. Slot indices start at zero and may differ from GUI order; a combined chest uses west/north-half-first ordering. Replaces the previous slot restriction while preserving the selected side; leaves the original handle unchanged. Does not bypass face visibility or transfer permissions. Slot restrictions are invalid for redstone queries. The method name ignores case.

redstone.description: Read the maximum native Redstone Port input level across all selected ports and faces of a LABEL_REF. Omitted side selects all six faces; slot restrictions are invalid. Missing, unloaded, disconnected, unsupported or incomplete access faults instead of returning zero. Provider errors and exhausted work limits also fault. This is separate from the manager's bare REDSTONE condition. The method name ignores case.
redstone.example:
let port = label("signal").side("north")
if (port.redstoneAvailable()) then
  print(port.redstone())
end

powered.description: Return whether the maximum native Redstone Port input level for the selected LABEL_REF ports/faces is greater than zero. Uses the same access contract as redstone(): unavailable access faults rather than returning false. Slot restrictions are invalid; omitted side selects all six faces. The method name ignores case.
powered.example:
let port = label("signal")
if (port.redstoneAvailable() and port.powered()) then
  print("Signal is high")
end

redstoneavailable.description: Check that every selected native Redstone Port and face is present, connected, loaded and readable. Missing, unsupported or incomplete access returns false; provider errors and exhausted work limits fault. Slot restrictions are invalid. This is the native signal endpoint check; ordinary available() checks item inventory access. The method name ignores case.
redstoneavailable.example:
let port = label("signal").side("north")
if (port.redstoneAvailable()) then
  print(port.redstone())
end

favailable.description: True only when every selected tank is available. Missing/incomplete groups return false. Defaults to FLUID("*"); only FLUID selectors are accepted. .side() selects a physical face. .slots() is invalid. Ambiguous views across faces require one explicit side.

fempty.description: True when a complete available group contains zero matching fluid. Missing/incomplete groups return false. Defaults to FLUID("*"); only FLUID selectors are accepted. .side() selects a physical face. .slots() is invalid. Ambiguous views across faces require one explicit side.

fcount.description: Sum matching millibuckets once per tank; unavailable/incomplete groups fault. Defaults to FLUID("*"); only FLUID selectors are accepted. .side() selects a physical face. .slots() is invalid. Ambiguous views across faces require one explicit side.

fcontents.description: Immutable per-tank rows: fluid (exact fluid/NBT key), id, amount (mB), dimension, x, y, z, tank, sideMask. Unavailable/incomplete groups fault. No reservation or persistent STATE. Defaults to FLUID("*"); only FLUID selectors are accepted. .side() selects a physical face. .slots() is invalid. Ambiguous views across faces require one explicit side.

nbtlength.description: Read captured ITEM_KEY NBT only; no live provider access or writes. JSON Pointer paths start with /; empty path selects root, ~1 escapes / and ~0 escapes ~. hasnbt returns false for missing paths; nbttype returns missing or the exact NBT type. Typed getters fault on missing/wrong type: nbtinteger reads byte/short/int/long without truncation, nbtstring requires string, nbttext displays scalar values including floats. nbtkeys returns sorted compound keys as string[] (max 256); nbtlength counts compound/list/array entries or UTF-16 string units. Paths max 512 characters/16 segments; shared work/allocation limits apply. Byte/int arrays and lists use zero-based indices. Use group.item from contents(), not an ITEM selector.
